## Technical Summary

* **Objective:** Serve as Inset 3 of the Map 7 tryptic (Zoom 3), transitioning from the regional Bight of California into the immediate coastal context of the UCSB campus and Goleta Slough.
* **Key Packages:** `terra`, `tidyverse`, `tidyterra`, `sf`
* **Data Sources:**
  * Campus DEM (`source_data/campus_DEM.tif`)
  * Campus hillshade (`source_data/campus_hillshade.tif`)
  * Offshore bathymetry (`output_data/campus_bath_epsg2874.tif`)
  * Campus buildings footprint (`source_data/campus_buildings/Campus_Buildings.shp`)
  * Isla Vista building structures (`source_data/iv_buildings/iv_buildings/CA_Structures_ExportFeatures.shp`)
  * Bike path centerlines (`source_data/icm_bikes/bike_paths/bikelanescollapsedv8.shp`)
  * NCOS Multi-use Trails (`source_data/ncos_trails/ncos_multiuse_trails.geojson`)
* **Styling Decisions:**
  * 4 wide x 3 tall landscape aspect ratio (`width = 4, height = 3`) matching the Map 7 row 1 layout.
  * Axis labels, coordinate text, and tick marks removed.
  * Legend omitted (`guide = "none"`, `legend.position = "none"`).
  * White background set explicitly in `ggsave` for consistent rendering.

---

## Step-by-Step Cartographic Workflow & Intermediate Outputs

The script `scripts/map_05.R` documents the systematic construction of Inset 3 (Zoom 3) across 6 intermediate visual iterations.

### Step 1: Base Raster Layers — DEM & Hillshade Inspection

Before combining layers, the script inspects the raw campus digital elevation model and the multidirectional hillshade raster individually.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
![Intermediate Output 5.1: Campus hillshade rendered in grayscale](../images/map5.1.png){fig-alt="Map 5.1 Campus Hillshade" width="100%"}
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
![Intermediate Output 5.2: UCSB DEM rendered with viridis gradient](../images/map5.2.png){fig-alt="Map 5.2 UCSB DEM" width="100%"}
:::
:::

### Step 2: Intermediate Plot — Layer Blending & Graticule Tests

Next, the hillshade is placed over the DEM using an alpha transparency aesthetic (`scale_alpha(range = c(0.05, 0.5))`), followed by removing axis tick marks to prepare for inset tiling.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
![Intermediate Output 5.3: Alpha-blended hillshade over DEM](../images/map5.3.png){fig-alt="Map 5.3 Alpha Blending" width="100%"}
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
![Intermediate Output 5.4: Stripping coordinate text and axis labels](../images/map5.4.png){fig-alt="Map 5.4 No Axis Labels" width="100%"}
:::
:::

### Step 3: Integrating Offshore Bathymetry, Buildings & Bikeways

Onshore elevation alone left the Pacific Ocean blank white. By incorporating the bathymetry raster, coastal contours blend seamlessly with onshore topography. Vector layers for campus buildings, Isla Vista structures, and campus and NCOS bikeways are overlaid to ground the terrain, and the subtitle is removed for a cleaner locator presentation.

```r
# Incorporating bathymetry, buildings, and bike paths
zoom_3_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = zoom_3_DEM_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = greatercampusDEM_1_1)) +
  geom_raster(data = campus_bath_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = bathymetry)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "NA", guide = "none") +
  geom_raster(data = zoom_3_hillshade_df, aes(x = x, y = y, alpha = hillshade)) +
  scale_alpha(range = c(0.05, 0.4), guide = "none") +
  geom_sf(data = iv_buildings, color = alpha("gray70", 0.2), fill = NA, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = buildings, color = "pink", fill = alpha("pink", 0.4), linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = bikeways, color = "#00abff", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_sf(data = ncos_trails, color = "#00abff", linewidth = 0.4) +
  my_theme +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) + 
  ggtitle("UCSB Surroundings")
```
